process_observations.observation: Runnability was taken from build_plan.py next rather than re-derived: M3-S03 was the single entry it printed, with its three dependencies M1-S01, M2-S04 and M3-S02 all documented and no step gate in the way.

Every claim in steps[M3-S03].inputs.note that could be checked from disk held: case-management-setup/references/metadata-examples.md exists and carries six XML fences, section 3 does say both channel blocks go in the same physical file, and the undeclared email-to-case checker does exit 1 on three WARNs of which two are unclearable from metadata.

The one decision this step was told not to pre-empt was structurally impossible to pre-empt anyway - EmailToCaseRoutingAddress has no sender field - and the two sender-adjacent switches that do exist in the same file, useSystemEmailAddress and isPermsetControlled, were omitted with the D-M3S02-04 reference recorded rather than defaulted.

Three consecutive steps now write a deploy-order.md that their outputs[] does not declare - M3-S01, M3-S02 and M3-S03 - so check-outputs has never confirmed the file the human's deploy actually reads.

reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M3.md and reports/mock-deploy/2026-09-12T04-14-39Z/ were written by another process about ninety seconds before this step was claimed, and the report's closing line already describes M3-S03 as running - so a second actor is reading this build directory while the loop runs.

The owning agent was executed inline rather than through the Agent tool, which is metadata-builder AGENT.md Step 6's 'any other host' branch and was the caller's explicit instruction; the run record and both envelopes are identical in shape either way, but the isolation a subagent would have given was not present.
